meta.description: Canonical accelerator skill list for Primary School Years. Small set of skills to act as course→ETP anchors for seeding and UI workflows.

accelerators.name: Focused Attention
accelerators.short_description: Sustain attention on a single task for increasing intervals.

accelerators.name: Working Memory
accelerators.short_description: Hold and manipulate small amounts of information in mind (2–5 items).

accelerators.name: Phonemic Awareness
accelerators.short_description: Hear, segment and blend sounds in spoken words (pre-literacy).

accelerators.name: Number Sense
accelerators.short_description: Internalise small quantities, simple comparisons and number relationships.

accelerators.name: Social Cooperation
accelerators.short_description: Share, take turns and collaborate effectively in small groups.

accelerators.name: Self-Regulation
accelerators.short_description: Manage impulses, calm down after frustration and follow multi-step instructions.

accelerators.name: Fine Motor Control
accelerators.short_description: Control small hand movements for writing, cutting and drawing.

accelerators.name: Problem-Solving Starter
accelerators.short_description: Approach simple puzzles and problems using trial, reason and explanation.

accelerators.name: Verbal Reasoning
accelerators.short_description: Interpret spoken instructions and explain reasoning using sentences.

accelerators.name: Digital Literacy
accelerators.short_description: Basic, safe use of educational devices and simple tools (typing, searching).

accelerators.name: Executive Function
accelerators.short_description: Plan, start and complete short multi-step tasks; monitor outcomes.

accelerators.name: Emotional Awareness
accelerators.short_description: Recognise and label basic emotions in self and others.

notes: Use these accelerator skills as small canonical seeds. Each item includes suggested ETP links that should be validated by domain experts before bulk seeding. Keep the set intentionally small to make course→ETP anchoring lightweight.
